newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan bourse index lower for second week.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan bourse index lower for second week.

text.p: The Casablanca stock exchange ended the week lower for the second consecutive week, due mainly to market volatility and the drop of blue-chip stocks, brokers said.
The all-share index closed at 434.37 points, down from 435.19 points last Friday.
Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur, one of the market's largest capitalisation stocks, lost five dirhams in one week to close at 395 dirhams.
Wafabank, a liquid stock, was traded at 530 dirhams, losing seven dirhams in one week.
"The bourse index decline over the past four days was largely due to an increased volatility in the market and to profit taking by foreign institutions," a market analyst at Upline Securities said.
Upline Securities has an index (USI 10) which tracks the most liquid stocks on the bourse.
The bourse was closed on Monday due to a public holiday.
Societe Nationale d'Investissement, Morocco's second largest private conglomerate closed at 558, down from 560 dirhams last week.
SNI has diversified stakes in more than 40 companies.
The Casablanca Finance Group index (CFG.25), which tracks the 25 most liquid stocks, closed at 6,889.88 points, down from 6,920.19 points last Friday.
Traded volume on the official market was 38.8 million dirhams compared with 15.9 million dirhams last Friday.
